If you now press the space bar (space) you will come back to the previously mentioned picture and the next player will be shown and can make his selection. If you answer the question correctly, 100 points will be credited to the respective account and the box will be filled with the color in which the respective player name is written. There is a bonus if you have correctly answered all questions in the three boxes in a row, column or diagonal. This bonus is indicated by these three boxes flashing in different colors.

161952.overview: This is another pinball game where you play 3 balls simultaneously, created by Jim McGue using Olaf Lubeck's Pinball Construction Set and published in PCS Club Disk #38.

162792.overview: Navigate a maze in a first person perspective. The player's task is to get out of a single or multi-story maze in the shortest possible time. At the beginning, the player declares the size of the maze, the number of floors 1-9 and the number of possible maps to be displayed.

162797.overview: Classic Pac-Man but in a 3D version. The player's task is to collect all the lozenges found in the maze. Four of them allow you to devour enemy creatures for a short time. On the right side of the screen you can see a small maze to help determine the player's location. Released in Compute mit 1986/08.

164146.overview:
Far in the future earth is dependent on silicon for it's technology. Unfortunately the silicon reserves are running out. A new source of silicon has been located in a faraway part of the galaxy. Problem is that it's very dangerous to gather since it has a tendency to explode. Therefore a mercenary going by the name of Sillo is sent to the location with a vehicle known as the silicon fisher to gather this necessary yet dangerous material.

3D Silicon Fish consists of a maze that is located above a river that floats from the top to the bottom of the screen. The player navigates through the maze with his vehicle while looking for silicon that floats with the stream. Collecting the silicon is done by positioning the vehicle towards the part where the silicon will pass and throwing out a net to catch it. The player is however not alone in the maze. Around him something called kryllon forms out of thin air and explodes after a short while. If the player then is within range of the explosion he will be killed.

164452.overview: 1 Block Sanke public domain snake game written in BASIC using only 1 block of memory iin 2004 by Diego Barzon.

166089.overview:
A collection of 3 games; Pontoon, a card game that is a relative of blackjack. British pontoon uses the terms "twist" (hit), "stick" (stand) and "buy" (double the bet, not to be confused with doubling down) and a different set of rules. The rules for buying in pontoon include allowing the player to buy on any hand of 2 to 4 cards, allowing the player to twist after he buys.

Roulette: In the game, players may choose to place bets on either a single number or the colors red or black, . To determine the winning number and color, a croupier spins a wheel in one direction, then spins a ball in the opposite direction around a tilted circular track running around the outer edge of the wheel. The ball eventually loses momentum, passes through an area of deflectors, and falls onto the wheel and into one of 20 numbered and colored slots (not the normal 37 or 
8). 

Aces High: Deal four cards, face up, one onto each tableau pile. If two or more of those cards have the same suit, move the lower-ranked ones onto the discard. When you can make no more moves, deal four more cards onto the tableaus, fanned down so that you can see the cards underneath. Only the topmost card of each tableau is available. Continue to move cards to the discard if they match the suit of any higher-ranked available card. If a pile is emptied, you must fill it with an available card from another tableau before you can deal again.

166161.overview: Careful cave exploration in your flying ship, watch the fuel meter and go fast enough to get to the next refueling station but watch out for the traps and lasers left around to stifle your journey. If you hit the walls or a laser beam, you will start at the screen entrance. Getting to the next screen does NOT replenish your fuel supplies, so you'd better hope the fueling station is close. A game created by Arne Jansen and Harald Beine and published in 64'er 1985/05.

166226.overview: Five Card Stud is a poker game using Nevada-rules Five-card-stud. The player must bet on their cards based on their value and the perceived value of the cards of the opponents.

166256.overview:
A two player only German language puzzle game. 18 Uhren (18 Clocks) was coded by Günter Kramer and published on Commodore Disk #39.
The game board consists of 18 clocks connected by eight rotating mechanisms. The computer randomly places yellow dots on each clock, and the player's task is probably to set these dots in the 12:00 o'clock position. To do this, you need to use the mechanisms to rotate the dials of the clocks. The problem is that the mechanisms are connected to the clocks diagonally, and in order to rotate the dials of the others you need to change their mode to on by pressing the shot button. In this mode, all clock faces connected to the mechanism will rotate. Mechanisms switched on next to each other will also be connected to each other, giving you endless possibilities for combinations.

166909.overview:
1000 Miler v2.0 is based on the French card games called Mille Bornes. Two players compete against each other to reach 1000 miles before the other. Each player gets seven cards, which can be miles cards for getting closer to your goal or positive or negative cards. Negative cards can be played to cause a flat tire for your opponent, letting him have a crash or other effects. The positive cards can be used to negate the effects of negative cards the opponent played on you. The winning player gets a little winning animation.

This version is an updated version of the original 1987 release with improved computer AI for single player games, and a few minor annoying bugs that were in the original were also removed.

This version was released on Loadstar #88.

166924.overview: 100 Racchette  (100 Rackets) is an  Italian language brain teaser/puzzle game published in Commodore Computer Club #08 (1984/01) The game has a maximum of 9 players (alternating turns).

167020.overview: 000 White Dash is a Boulder Dash clone developed by Thomas "Firefox" Schaub using Peter Liepa's Boulder Dash Construction Kit in 2015.

167027.overview: 17+4 (or 17 und 4) is the German name for the English card game blackjack. A classic game of mesh, in which one must get no more than 21 points. The player draws cards and if the sum of card values exceeds 21, the player loses. This version was developed in 1991 by Manfred Scholz and published in the January '92 issue of 64'er magazine.

167289.overview: An educational French language teaching game developed by Michael Quigley and published by COMPUTE! Publications, Inc. in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/04 (Issue #10). It was also published in COMPUTE!'s Commodore Collection - Vol.2.

167315.overview:
10k is a German language turn-based  dice game created by Moritz Weissbrich for the  2nd 4k BASIC Compo in 2009. 
A game for 255 players, where the winner is the one who scores 10000 points. Before the turn begins, the software draws six digits representing the dice eyes. The player can collect ones, fives and threes of identical digits by pressing the corresponding keys displayed at the bottom of the screen. The key symbols correspond to the German names of the digits and are arranged in order from 1 to 6, i.e., E, Z, D, V, F, S. Collecting three threes gives 300 points, three sixes 600 points, and so on. Only collecting three ones gives 1000 points. After collecting the dice, the player can throw the remaining dice again by pressing the W key until all of them have been collected or if no longer possible. In the latter case, the points will not be added to the player's score. By pressing the B key, the player ends his turn by taking the points scored.

167317.overview: A game created by a guy known only as Sovereign using Chris Yates' Shoot em Up Construction Kit  that follows in the traditional 1942ish SHMUP style.

167613.overview: 3D Crosshairs style space-themed blasting action created using SEUCK but using the software in a very different way to that point. 3D Space Wars is an Operation Wolf-style blaster but one that is set in a galaxy far, far away. You control the laser targeter using your joystick and blast away at anything that moves, and there is a LOT of movement.

167686.overview:
This is a computerized version of the card game 21 (also known as Blackjack). It was developed by Scott Hossner. The year of release and publisher  is currently unknown.
A classic game of Blackjack, in which one should get no more than 21 points. At the beginning, the player declares the value of his wallet, the difficulty level determining the value of the computer opponent's wallet and sets the betting rate. Then he draws cards to get the value closest to winning, i.e. 21 points. If this value is exceeded, the player loses and loses the pledged money. Winning against the opponent guarantees a prize in the amount of the declared bet stake. Losing all the funds of any player ends the game.

167687.overview: A text based blackjack game developed in BASIC by Timothy Orr Knight, and Darren LaBatt, and published as a type in by Howard W. Sams & Co., Inc. in their book "Commodore 64 BASIC Programs".

167816.overview:
1k-mini-bdash is a clone of Boulder Dash, crammed into 1024 bytes. Like in the original, you have to collect diamonds while avoiding falling boulders and deadly fireflies; to exit a level, you have to collect at least a specific amount of diamonds. According to the author, there are, 1024 different levels in the game.

It was created by Simon Stelling in 2008 for the Minigame Competition 2008 - 1K Category / 1024 Bytes Game Compo 2nd Edition.

167832.overview: 25 Dollar is a public domain game developed in 1998 by "Wusel" It is a breakout clone, but instead of bricks you have to remove dollar signs.

167833.overview: A 2-player only tron light cycles game developed by Colt Seavers in 2009 for the 4k BASIC Compo.

167835.overview:
This is a German language maze escape game developed by Ulrich Faßbender in 1988 and published by Markt & Technik in Happy Computer 1989/01.
The player's task is to get out of two mazes in the shortest possible time while avoiding red creatures. Each collision with a creature adds penalty points.

167837.overview: 3Peak x 10Lines is a solitaire card game developed by Gary Lake-Schaal for the 2015 BASIC Tenliners competition. A relaxing solitaire-style card game in which, to win, you must collect all the cards from the table and arrange them into three pyramids. To do this, you must draw a card that is one rank higher or lower than the card shown at the bottom. If you cannot draw such a card, you must turn over the next card from the bottom row by pressing the arrow button. If you manage to collect all the cards, the game ends in victory and the next round begins. The game ends when it is no longer possible to collect all the cards from the table because there are no more cards to turn over.

167838.overview: A Danish language computerized rendition of the classic four-in-a-row/connect four game. Developed by Anders Jensen and published by IC RUN in LIST! 1988/1.

167843.overview:
A public domain Minesweeper clone made by Chill in 2001 for the Minigame Competition 2001 - 2K Category.

A classic Sapper, in which based on the displayed numbers indicating the number of mines around them, the player marks the potential location of a mine. The remaining fields where there are no mines should be completely uncovered. Discovering all fields where there are no mines guarantees victory in the game. Uncovering a field with a mine detonates it.

168413.overview:
1nvader is very simple yet challenging space shooter developed by Darren Foulds in 2019 for the Commodore 64. It's similar to Space Invaders except you have only one alien invader to kill. However, as a result of this, the single invader is made harder to kill than the invaders in the typical Space Invaders clone, making the game a bit more challenging. 
 
Released as part of the Single Button Games Collection by BOBR Games.

168422.overview: A simple 1 on 1 shooter in which you try to kill the computer (or 2nd player) opponent created by Explora Commodore and published by Matra Games Corp. in 2019. Coded by Darro99 with Igor Errazkin on graphics, and Narciso Quintana Varo who did the SFX and music.

168891.overview:
This one is based on a mathematics game theory problem for 100 people, but the game simulates the problem with just one player.

The computer selects a random number from 1 to 100 as your lucky number. You will need to guess which box from 00-99 where the lucky number is hidden. The game allows you to have up to 50 guesses, but it's not easy to win as it sounds!

Published as part of the 2018 C64 4KB Game Coding Competition

171826.overview:
Most football management games written for 64K/48K computers concentrated their memory space on providing as many features as possible for a lone player. As the title implies, this game is an exception - 2 players each take control of a club, taking it in turns to make their managerial decisions and play their matches. For an extra competitive edge, they can include their own name among the players (which are otherwise made up of the real players of the day).

The game uses a fictional 20-team superleague, with English and Scottish clubs, as well as a knock-out cup. You can buy or sell players, who have ability ratings out of 15, and swap your squad of 19 around to choose 11 starters plus 2 substitutes. Match scores are listed along with goalscorers, although the scorers update more quickly than the scores. You are kept up to date with financial changes after each match.

172629.overview:
The 7 Doctors (or The Seven Doctors) is a z-machine based text adventure based on The popular BBC Science Fiction series Doctor Who. The original was written by David Burke in 2018. The Commodore 64 version was converted by Scott Breon via a Z-Machine conversion website in 2019.

In this game you play the seventh incarnation of The Doctor (Sylvester McCoy). Various enemies have kidnapped and imprisoned your other six previous incarnations, and it's up to you to save each and every one of them, for if you don't your death becomes a fixed point in time.

172750.overview: 1917 is an arcade game set in Lenin's time. The player's task is to perform a series of tasks that will eventually lead to a communist revolution. As Lenin, the player must avoid or kill numerous assassins (with a gun with unlimited ammo) and mechanical traps.

173158.overview:
A puzzle game loosely featuring licensing from the 7Up soft drink. The gameplay involves up to 4 players, which can be either human or computer, each taking on spots of a particular colour. Starting from opposite corners, they take it in turns to move, either by 'reproducing' one of their spots to form another one in an adjacent square, or by making a jump, losing the square you did have but taking one two spaces away.

When a piece lands next to one of another colour, that piece changes colour into that of their opponent. The winner of each round is either the last player with any pieces left, or the player who has the most pieces left when the level is full.

175334.overview:
This is a game developed by Australian based coder Barry Hart (aka Cout) for the 2016 C64 4KB Game Coding Competition. It was coded entirely in BASIC.

The goal of the game is to press beat the high score by pressing a key (any key) before the clock runs out. The closer you press the key to the count of zero (the clock fades and disappears before the count of four, thus adding to the challenge) In this game, the LOWER the number of the score, the better.

175936.overview: A well-made version of the popular puzzle game of the same name made by Per Anders Bäckström (a member of TRIAD) This version was released for free in 2014.

178387.overview:
10 Great Games II is a compilation containing the following ten games:

•  Auf Wiedersehen Monty
•  Basil the Great Mouse Detective
•  Bulldog
•  ConvoyRaider
•  Death Wish 3
•  Jack the Nipper in Coconut Capers
•  MASK
•  Re-Bounder
•  Samurai Trilogy
•  Thing Bounces Back

178388.overview:
Gremlin's third compilation of ten games differs from the first and second in that the games featured were not originally by Gremlin themselves apart from Re-Bounder:

•  10th Frame
•  Firelord
•  Rana Rama
•  Leader Board
•  Iridis Alpha
•  Re-Bounder
•  Alleykat
•  Eagles
•  Last Mission
•  Fighter Pilot

178389.overview:
30 Games is a collection of games that contains the following:

•  Astral Zone
•  Cosmic Convoy
•  Milky Way
•  Phase 4
•Detective
•  Robocity
•  Invasion
•  Micromouse
•  Orion Quest
•  Poster Paster
•  Gyropod
•  Quintic Warrior
•  Valley
•  Transector
•  3D Tunnel
•  Bozo
•  Demon Knight
•  Jammin
•  Savage Pond
•  Lander
•  Seaside Special
•  Timezone
•  Strontium Dog
•  Super Gridder
•  20 Tons
•  Schizofrenia
•  Pipeline
•  Up, Up, and Away
•  Bismark
•  Escape

A good portion of the games were previously released under different names.

178416.overview: With 4th & Inches Team Construction Disk, you can create the ultimate player and the ultimate team. Assign all the stats, sizes and playing characteristics of each of your 4th & Inches players. Pit real-life pros against a team made up of your friends. Name your team, choose the jersey color and then save it to disk. The possibilities are endless.

179076.overview:
5th in the Revision 2019 Game competition. A Karate fighting game for head to head competition. Super 1337! Y0u r34lly 5h0uld 7ry 17!
Karate fights for two players in eight different settings. You can also play against a computer opponent. Depending on your choice, winning depends on the number of winning fights 2-5.

179106.overview: 360 ARM is a SEUCK shooter developed by Shaun Pearson in 2004. It was published by TND and also published in GO64! 2005/04.

179260.overview:
4th Dimension is a collection of four games that contains the following:

•Cyberdyne Warrior: A flick screen platform shooter where you are a Cyberdyne Warrior and your mission is to visit three planets to capture escaped robots from the prisons that orbit the planets. The robots were in prison due to breaking one of Isaac Asimov's Robotic Laws, but due to the amount breaking the law, the original prison was overcrowded, so three more were built to house them. Now the robots have started escaping and you must move around each level shooting other robots and creatures as well as capture a robot. Once you have captured a robot you are transported to a shop to upgrade yourself and weapons, and these are paid for by collecting money found scattered on each level. There are also other obstacles that need avoiding like water and fire and if you touch these or are hit then you lose part of an energy bar. Once this is empty then it is game over.

•Head the Ball: A scrolling platform game where the screen scrolls from left to right when you move, as you control a head who has to bounce to the end of each level in his mission to rescue his girlfriend. She has been taken by the Globoid Hells Angels and as you move through a level, you have to collect enough gems to trade for your girlfriend. There are various creatures on each level and these must be avoided or shot with limited bullets, and if you touch one or fall off the bottom of the screen then you lose one of five lives and sent back to the start of the level. You are armed also with a shield and two smart bombs, and the level must be completed within a time limit. Once you reach a heart at the end of a level you are transported to a bonus level which is a side view single screen shooter where you must blast various waves of alien ships.

•Insects in Space: A horizontal scrolling shooter inspired by the arcade game Defender, where the screen scrolls left or right when you move Saint Helen as you try to stop bees from grabbing babies. You must shoot all the bees with your laser eyes as they try to swoop down and take the various babies to the top of the screen. If a baby is taken in the air then the bee can still be shot and the baby caught before it hits the ground. Above the playing area is a radar and this shows you the position of the babies, bees and various other creatures. The other creatures can be shot or avoided and if you are hit then you lose one of three lives. You also are equipped with three smart-bombs which kills all on the screen when activated.

•Mission Impossibubble: A isometric platform game where the screen scrolls when you move your hero, a bubble with a face that moves along the maze of platforms over various levels. Your mission is to rescue six baby bubbles but to do this you first have to collect eight pieces of a scroll on each level before you can get the baby and lead it back to your starting position.

180293.overview:
3D maze game developed by Tommi Timonen and published in MikroBitti magazine. Issue 1986/09.
The player's task is to find the exit from the maze in the shortest possible time. While wandering, a map can be turned on, which shows the exit but not the player's location.

180491.overview: A five card draw poker game developed by D.M. Arnel and published by Binary Zone PD in 1985.

180606.overview: Known as both 4 Aces Pinball and Poker of Aces, this pinball table, created with the Pinball Construction Set features a playing card motif. Score more points that your opponent or exceeding your personal best is the goal of this game. It is up to you to keep the ball in the field by bouncing it against the buffers and hitting the targets to score as many points as possible. Try to send the ball into the side corridor where the word POKER appears, to ear bonus points and hit as many targets as possible before you lose all 5 balls. Published in Italy as Poker D'Assi in the Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - mega collection (1985).

180613.overview: The 64 Speller is an educational spelling game developed by Gary V. Fields and published in RUN 1984/09 (Issue #9) and also in Stonysoft #1748.

181851.overview:
Atari 800 XL/Commodore 64 flippy disk. This compilation contains two shoot-em-ups:

•    L.A. Swat
•    Panther

182420.overview: 007 Ja Tohtori Ei (which translates into 007 and Dr No)  is a James Bond themed text adventure in the Finnish language. Written and released by Jari Saarhelo in 1983.

182421.overview: The '04 Lucky Poker Game is a slot machine game written entirely in BASIC. It was developed by Australian based coder Barry "Cout" Hart in 2004.

182459.overview: Play against a friend or the C64, or watch a demonstration mode of the C64 vs ZX SPECTRUM. The object of the game is to simply match 4 counters in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally to win the game. The opponent can also do that :)

184498.overview: A puzzle game where time is the key (at least on the face of things) created by Kopido Games and published in both Game On 1992/09, and in Game On GE 1993/1.

188828.overview:
“3 Days” was originally to be the sequel to the popular “Valkyrie 17” game by George Stone and The Ramjam Corp.

The game was to be a text adventure, which was written using “The Biro”. Featuring character set screens, livened up with moving sprites (Including a dodo which fixated on you as its mother when it hatched), the game was shaping up well. All words in the adventure were in Carpathian, until you found a dictionary in the game.

Promising indeed, though it is unknown why it was never released, or even how far exactly it got. Its unlikely that it was finished, due to sources revealed below. Ram Jam were never too popular after the dire “Explorer” game they released for Electric Dreams, but with the guy mentioned next, maybe they were finally onto something…

192118.overview:
The 1984 Atarisoft collection for the Commodore 64 was created by Bandit Breaking Service and includes all the AtariSoft games for the C64 with the exception of Battlezone and Galaxian, and the unreleased/leaked versions of Mario Brothers and Joust. Games included:

◉ Centipede
◉ Defender
◉ Dig Dug
◉ Donkey Kong
◉ Jungle Hunt
◉ Moon Patrol
◉ Ms. Pacman
◉ Pac-Man
◉ Pole Position
◉ Robotron: 2084

192141.overview: 1, 2, 3 is a pinball game with three playfields one above the other. The ball can be sent into the next playfield and you attempt to keep it there using that playfields flippers. The higher playfields yield higher points.

194921.overview:
421 is a French language dice-based gambling game for 1-2 players. It was developed by J. Gaits and published in Hebdogiciel N°009 (09.12.1983).
A dice game for one or two players. Each has a number of his chips, which he pays with depending on the scores of the hands shown at the bottom of the screen. During your turn, you can swap one or two of the three dice twice to increase your score. After exchanging only one cube, press the ENTER key. The game ends when one player loses all his chips.

194923.overview:
You are the pilot of a new spaceship. You must tet the craft to its limits. You can fly along the canyon and through the space maze. The ship will change color to warn of changes in the canyon size. At teh end of your flight you will be ranked. You must not hit the sides of the canyon, but asteroids will fly by. Good luck! 
 
 
Published as part of the "Star Fighter" game pack, COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1984/01 (Issue #07) / no definite name, game says "64-Canyon".

197678.overview: 3-D-Autorennen is a German language driving game. It's not so much a racer per se as it is a game in which you must dodge other cars for as long as you can.  It was developed by Rüdiger Linden and published as a type-in by Data Becker GmbH in their book "C64 Superspiele selbstgemacht" in 1985.

197687.overview: 3-Gewinnt is a 1-2 player German language interpretation of Tic-Tac-Toe/Noughts and Crosses for the C64. It was developed by KWJ and released into the public domain in 1986.

198027.overview: 1916 is a Spanish-language war strategy game for one player, whose task is to destroy eight German cities using available bombs. Depending on the size of the city, more bombs will need to be dropped to destroy it. If the bombs run out and at least one undestroyed city remains, the game will end in defeat.

199015.overview: 1-2-3... is a public domain text adventure developed by Chris Mudd for the 2000 Interactive Fiction Competition.

201385.overview: 4k-BASIC-Dash is a Boulder Dash clone coded entirely in BASIC by Simon Stelling in 2009. It was released as part of the 2nd 4k BASIC Compo.

201387.overview: A game for 1-9 players, where the winner is the one who scores 5000 points. Before the turn begins, the software draws six digits representing the dice eyes. The player can collect ones, fives and threes of identical digits. Collecting three threes gives 300 points, three sixes 600 points, etc. Only collecting three ones gives 1000 points. The player successively collects the cubes by pressing the J key until all the cubes have been collected or until there are no more cubes. In the latter case, the points will not be added to the player's score.

204645.overview: Released in 1984, League Soccer is a mail-order only game by Sophisticated Games designed to simulate a soccer season. The player is able to configure a league with between 2 and 24 teams of their choice. Each team is given a rating between 1 and 9 which will affect their ability throughout the game and can be given a name of up to 8 characters. The main menu gives you several options and the first gives you the ability to simulate a week of the season. This will show you all of the games for that week and allow you to give a score out of 100 which will bias the chances of the home team. This will default to a value based on the ratings of the teams involved but can be adjusted if required.

205394.overview:
162 Police are in action. As one of the 162 police officers you must rid the city of criminal gangs. Simply by shooting at them. Can you put an end to the big crime wave, and restore peace and justice back to the community? Your job is to protect and serve the public, after all.

Developed by Roberto Ricioppo using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit in 2016.

205441.overview:
Despite the chessboard, 8 Enemy Queens is not a chess game, rather it's a brain-teaser/logical puzzle game in which you have to uncover 8 queens without running into any conflicts. Not as easy as it seems.

This game was developed by Ismail Sahin and released into the public domain in 2003. However, it was also released in the following:

•   GO64! 2005/04
•   GO64! 2005/05

207068.overview:
Complete rows or columns using the Tetris-style blocks to clear them. You score one point per square filled, and can clear multiple columns or rows in one move to score bonuses. 

When no moves are possible, the game ends. Getting a high score will involve careful planning to make sure you don't leave yourself with a block that cannot be placed!

This game is based on a mobile game called 1010. However, the developer added a number of extra Tetris pieces that aren't in the mobile version, which increases the difficulty and gives more variety to the gameplay.

Developed by Nick "Arlasoft" Sherman and released on his itch.io page on February 20, 2020.

207128.overview:
An overhead racing game created by Anthony Beaucamp . Welcome to the “8bit-Slicks”, a remake of the legendary 90s game. It is a game featuring:

    Up-to 4 players (local or online).
    10 varied maps (jumps, obsctales, cross-points).
    Online competitive ranking.
    A friendly community.

207294.overview:
105: One Oh Five is a blackjack variant for the C64. It was developed by Hugo van Galen and released into the public domain in 2020.
A card game of classic mesh but with changed rules for scoring points. Generally, you have to lay down cards in five piles in any way you want, so that you try to get 21 points on each pile. The last card laid that exceeds the total of 21 points on each stack ends the turn and the total number of points is counted. If a player gets less than 98 points in total then he loses one of his three lives. The upper right side of the screen shows the score calculated on the value of the sum of all cards from 98 to 105. In this range the player gets points added to the total score. Gaining points to the score starts a new turn and updates the scoring table with higher values each time. The game ends when the player loses all lives.

207424.overview:
20000 Beghe Sotto i Mari translates to "20000 quarrels at the bottom of the sea". 

You play as a treasure-hunting scuba diver that is constantly threatened by marine life. You can either shoot them with your harpoon or avoid them entirely while collecting the valuables literally floating around.

207972.overview: 2K Game-Creator is a German language game construction kit/engine for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Sven Forstmann and published in 64'er Sonderheft 94.

208011.overview: 3 Line Slot Machine is a public domain casino slot machine game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Carl M. Lockman and released in 1988.

208013.overview: 2048 is a conversion of the popular puzzle game of the same name for the Commodore 64. This version was developed by Johan van den Brande and released into the public domain in 2014.

208021.overview: 3-D Adventure is a 3D arcade adventure created with the 3D Construction Kit. 3 D Adventure is demo game which came with the 3D Construction Kit  for Commodore 64. 3DCK developed by Incentive Software and published by Domark, in 1991.

208443.overview: Welcome to the Year 2438, The Year the "Invaders" Return. A Shoot 'Em' Up Construction Kit Game for your C64, 1 or 2 Players created by TheReaperUK with music by Andrew Fisher.

209247.overview:
4 Most Horror is a compilation of the following four games:

•    NEIL Android (isometric action game)
•    Nosferatu the Vampyre (isometric action-adventure game)
•    The Rocky Horror Show (arcade adventure with puzzle elements)
•    She Vampires (vampire themed Gauntlet clone)

210535.overview:
31 is a single player German language dice game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Gerd Volk and released into the public domain in 1984.
A dice game in which a player reaching more than 31 minus points loses. Generally, in each round, one should try to get at least 30 points. If a player gains 27 points, he will receive 3 penalty points. Reaching, for example, 34 points results in the collection of all fours in successive tosses, until none of them fall out. The sum of the fours collected represents additional penalty points for the opponent. If the player collects 32 points, then twos are collected, and so on. The game itself consists of throwing the dice and collecting as many values as possible until the last dice is taken. Then the total of all dice and penalty points is counted.

210796.overview:
99 Luftballons is a strange little game for the Commodore 64, which also seems like a take on one of the Minigames in Lazy Jones and the game's name obviously inspired by the 80s German pop music hit of the same name. 

Grab the balloons to make it to your home at the top of the screen, as the ladder on the left-hand side of the screen is broken. There's a blue enemy that shoots arrows at the balloons to try to bust it while you're going up. 

The game was developed by Mario Walther and released into the public domain in 1985.

211621.overview:
3D Morris (also known as 3D Mühle) is a 1984 C64 game of unknown origin. It has a selectable language menu for either the English or German versions.
An expanded version of the tic-tac-toe game in which the player must arrange four of its symbols vertically, horizontally and diagonally. The game is played on four grids of 16 squares each.

213383.overview:
A Game for TheC64Maxi/C64Mini/Commodore 64 or a Good C64 Emulator.

Single-player fun arcade like shoot 'em' up. Fly your plane and shoot the other planes and boats. Fly into the balloons for bonus points.

Made by TheReaperUK using SEUCK.

214864.overview: Simply keep yourself on the track and don't hit the sides or outcroppings. Score increases based on your speed and time on the course. Coded by Spike78 and released in September of 2020.

215111.overview:
Not to be confused with KnockOut! from Alligata Software, which is a 2 player boxing game, 10...Knock Out! is a Finnish boxing game for 1 player only, developed by Jann Julkunen & Juha Granberg and published by AmerSoft in 1985.
Classic boxing, in which the player's task is to knock out the opponent. It is important to properly distribute the energy, which falls with each punch made. If the energy drops to zero then no punch can be made, and thus the fight will end in defeat. A knockout occurs when the energy exceeds 20 points. With each fight won, the difficulty level increases in the form of a stronger and smarter opponent.

217313.overview: 5x5 is a Polish language puzzle-board game for two players, based on the TV show called "5 on the 5". The player's task is to guess a five letter password in five attempts. After typing each password the game shows the result. Correctly guess a letter is highlighted with blue color, the letter appearing in the password in a different position is highlighted with yellow color. Number of performed trials decides who won the turn and who will start the next one.

217670.overview:
10tex is a simple western style "crosshair" shooter for the Commodore 64. It was coded entirely in BASIC by Back to the 8 Bit for the ASCII BASIC Game 2021 Compo.
The player takes on the role of a sheriff in the Wild West, who uses a crosshair to take out the villains as they appear. Every missed shot or delay in aiming results in the opponent landing a direct hit on the sheriff, which costs the player one of their three lives.

218242.overview:
Ten Great Games is a compilation from Gremlin Graphics. It includes the following 10 games:

Avenger
Bounder
Footballer of the Year
Future Knight
Highway Encounter
Jack the Nipper
Krakout
Monty on the Run
Trailblazer
West Bank

218831.overview: Despite it's name, 8-Ball is not a pool/billiards game, it's actually a pinball game with a very loose pool theme. The game was developed by an unknown person using Olaf Lubeck's Pinball Construction Set. it was released into the public domain as part of PCS Club Disk #29 in 1991.

219811.overview:
Move all the tiles in the grid to order them 1 to 8 from left to right, top to bottom.

Press the corresponding tile to move it into the empty space.

417748.overview: The player's task is to take over all the squares on the board within a certain time by painting paths around them. The paths are traversed by rubber bands carrying the player's ball to the start of the board and enemy spinning creatures, contact with which ends in loss of life. Fortunately, various bonuses appear in random places to add points, time, slow down or stop enemies for a while. There are also blocks that make the game more difficult such as adding a new enemy or losing a life. After completing a level, a stage involving obstacle avoidance will start, which lasts a set amount of time. Losing a life in this stage causes it to start again. The entire game contains 40 boards to complete and bosses appear in further stages.

418050.overview: A bowling game from Gary James and published in 2005. It was originally released at the Commodore 64 Crap Game Compo 2005 (C64CGC).

419905.overview: 1944 is a 1-2 player vertically scrolling cooperative shoot em up made via the Shoot 'Em Up Constructin Kit by GLI & Bose of The Criminal Empire. It was released sometime in December 1988.

420287.overview:
100: Hack the System (also known as Hack the System) is an education math game with puzzle elements similar in some ways to Mastermind, but with addition. You complete against the AI. The goal is to be the first to reach a sum of 100, hence the name of the game. 

The game was developed by B. Spartalis and published in PIXEL Junior #2 (01/1988).

420310.overview:
You're a skateboarder in Skate City, one of the largest skateparks ever built. Ollie off of ramps, grind on rails, and swerve past pedestrians as you bust out tricks. Visit skate shops scattered around the park to upgrade your gear and improve your skills. Participate in competitions to earn medals and cash to use in the shops. But, if you don't get to a competition in time, the infamous "Skate Or Die" message appears, and then you have to hurry!

There were two versions for the Commodore 64. One version was developed by Atari Games for the U.S./Canadian Market, and published by Mindscape, and the other version was developed by Tiertex for the European market and published by U.S. Gold in most of Europe, and by Erbe Software in Spain. This is the entry for the European version.

The graphics are considerably different in both versions, and the gameplay and controls being different in both versions as well.

424883.overview:
Three-dimensional space shooter. This is a modded version of Synapse Software's Sentinel, which was released four years prior.
The player takes on the role of the captain of a space battleship, and their task is to stop the alien invasion. To do this, they must use the map to select the sectors under attack. Alien units emerge from four large ships positioned in each corner of the map. To destroy the alien mother ship using proton bombs activated by the SPACE bar, you must navigate the space tunnel, ensuring that your ship is positioned within the elliptical field visible on the scanner. During combat, the player’s ship will often sustain serious damage. In this case, you must return to your own mothership by flying through the space tunnel, where you can carry out repairs and replenish your energy and shield strength. If the sector containing the player’s mothership is surrounded by sectors conquered by the aliens, an attack on it will commence. You must then clear these sectors before the mothership is destroyed. The game ends if the player defeats the aliens or their ship is destroyed.

424893.overview:
A SEUCK shooter by Alf Yngve, with music by Richard Bayliss. Our hero, the Master of Awesome, visits his mentor the Master of Exposition to congratulate him on his 113th birthday. He finds that his mentor's office has been blown up by enemies of the Temple of Awesome.

And so the Master of Exposition gives him a mysterious letter and a new quest: He must enter the Dojo of Doom and personally deliver the letter to the Master Ninja... (That's the setup -- the punchline comes at the very end of the game!)

This game was released in full commercial glory in the Kung Fu Maniacs Trilogy release.

425192.overview:
10Liner-Golf is a simple miniature golf game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Georg Rottensteiner (Barnsley Badger, Souless, Souless II, Joe Gunn, etc.) and released as part of the 2019 BASIC 10liner Contest.
A simple golf game in which the player enters the force with which to hit the ball in order to get it into the hole. The course is generated randomly each time and features grass, water and sand. If the ball lands behind the hole, a negative force value must be entered.

425198.overview:
10Lines Adv is a short text adventure written in BASIC for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Marco Spadaletti and released as part of the 2020 Basic 10Liner Contest.

The game has both English and German versions.

425326.overview:
A SEUCK game from TheReaperUK that tries to masquerade itself as an RPG. This was released into the public domain in 2020.
The player takes on the role of a knight armed with a sword who must escape from an underground complex full of traps and creatures. While wandering, you can collect treasure chests and vials of potions that add new life. A collision with any hostile creature ends tragically.

425354.overview: An interpretation of 1942 using the Shoot'em up Construction Kit, created by The Reaper UK with music by Andrew Fisher.

425385.overview: A tech demo game featuring the 8bit-Unity platform, a diablo-inspired dungeon crawler created by Anthony Beaucamp, the 8bit-Dude.

425458.overview:
Controls: use joystick in port 2
LEFT: to decrease the angle
RIGHT: to increse the angle
FIRE: to take a picture
For the real 'Pavel' experience I suggest you play with a pen/paper or a calculator and the PROBOS 2000 manual at hand, nothing else.
The professor had a heart attack and entrusted the cleaner with the very serious task of taking six photographs of the celestial body under study. The player, taking on the role of a random astronaut, must adjust the probe’s angle of inclination whilst flying at a distance of over 1,000 km from the planet in order to take the best possible photographs. The photographs will not turn out if the distance is less than 1,000 km or if the angle is incorrect. The screen displays the distance from the planet and from Earth. The probe travels at a speed of 100 km/s, whilst the data transmission speed is equal to the speed of light, i.e. just under 300,000 km/s. A negative distance value indicates that the probe is approaching the planet, whilst a positive value indicates that it is moving away. The best photo can be taken at a distance of -1,000 km at an angle of 45 degrees and at a distance of 1,000 km at an angle of 135 degrees, which is very difficult to achieve. Once all the photos have reached Earth, they can be viewed and, depending on their quality, the player will receive the appropriate number of points.

425459.overview: Race against the clock to create a 20 tile before the grid fills to the top. Combine tiles of the same value by smashing them into each other. Break linked tiles by combining one. A fast-paced puzzle game written for the 2022 Reset Magazine Craptastic Compo.

440040.overview: A classic mesh game in which no more than 21 points must be scored. Before drawing cards, the player determines the amount of the stake. Then he draws cards to get the value closest to winning, i.e. 21 points. If this value is exceeded, the player loses and loses the pledged money.

440048.overview: A classic mesh game in which no more than 21 points must be scored. Before drawing cards, each player determines the amount of the stake and places it in the pot. Then he draws cards to get the value closest to winning, which is 21 points. If this value is exceeded, the player loses and loses the pledged money.

440054.overview: A classic game of mesh, in which one should get no more than 21 points. At the beginning, the player declares the value of his wallet and sets the betting rate. Then he draws cards to get the value closest to winning, i.e. 21 points. If this value is exceeded, the player loses and loses the pledged money. Winning against the opponent guarantees a prize in the amount of the declared bet rate. Losing all funds ends the game.

440068.overview: A classic mesh game for two players in which no more than 21 points must be scored. Each player has six face-down cards in front of him and reveals any of them to reach the value closest to winning, which is 21 points. If this value is exceeded, the player automatically loses.

440071.overview: A classic blackjack game in which you must score no more than 21 points. The player draws cards and if the sum of the card values exceeds 21, the player loses. Also known as 17+4 Deluxe. Published in Digital Marketing PD #219.

440185.overview: The player's task is to reach the southeast corner of the maze in the shortest possible time to get out of it. The map can be turned on at any time, and movement is accomplished by pressing the direction name keys W, N, S, E and SPACE to take a step forward.

440222.overview: A game with the computer in which 23 matches lie on the table. In each turn you can take 1, 2 or 3 matches. Moves are made alternately with the computer and the loser is the one who has to take the last match.

440238.overview: A classic mesh game in which no more than 21 points must be scored. Before drawing cards, the player always pays £10. Then he draws cards to get the value closest to winning, which is 21 points. If this value is exceeded, the player loses and loses the pledged money. A win against the opponent guarantees a prize of £50. Losing all funds ends the game.

440298.overview: The player's task is to exit a randomly generated maze, created based on the parameters entered.

440364.overview: The player's task is to protect the planet from being destroyed by aliens. To do this, you need to shoot at the moving alien ships, directing the trajectory of the missile and shooting down their projectiles with the help of the sight. Each hit lowers the shield level of the defense platform and if it drops to zero, the planet will be destroyed.

440380.overview: The game is similar to the traditional game of tic-tac-toe, but is played on four 4×4 grids arranged vertically. To win, a player must place four of his symbols on four fields in a vertical, horizontal or diagonal pattern, either on a single grid or evenly distributed across all four grids. This gives a total of 76 possible ways to win.

440385.overview: A logical game of three-dimensional tic-tac-toe but with slightly different rules. In this version, the game does not end when you arrange your pawns three by three horizontally, vertically and diagonally, but only when all the fields are occupied by the players' symbols. At the end, the number of stacked threes is compared and the one with the most threes wins.

440408.overview:
A 4x4 game for two players. At the beginning you can choose a black and white or color version, and then the names of the players are introduced. The game board consists of 16 fields, on which players place their color blocks. Blocks can also be stacked on top of each other up to a maximum of four. The goal of the game is to lay four of your color blocks in a straight line horizontally, vertically and diagonally in any direction. You can swap players at any time with the F3 key or use the intuitive hint by pressing F1. 
 
Published in https://archive.org/details/64er_1984_12

440419.overview: The player's task is to avoid collisions with approaching obstacles. Every dozen or so obstacles avoided, the player moves on to the next, slightly more difficult stage. At the beginning of the game, the player chooses the speed of approaching obstacles from 1 to 5.

440483.overview:
A strategy game for two people in which four circles or crosses must be placed in a straight line horizontally or vertically to win. Each player chooses the number 1-9 or the letter A-I and places their symbol to the right next to the letter or at the bottom next to the number. Selecting the same letter or number moves the existing symbol up or to the left, respectively. In this way, more symbols are added until a winning line is laid. 
 
Published in the January 1991 issue of the German magazine 64'er.

440497.overview: A strategy game for two people in which four blocks of one color must be aligned horizontally, vertically or diagonally in any direction to win.

440517.overview: A two-player game in which the aim is to arrange your coloured five boxes vertically, horizontally and diagonally. During his turn, the player has the choice of painting any field on the board with a colour or moving any row or column by one field.

440570.overview:
Classic pinball, which with its theme refers to a club used the game of golf.

Developed by Charles M. Duncan and published in both:

- PCS Club Disk #07
- Stonysoft #1730

440597.overview: A puzzle game based on the Polish quiz show 5×5, the player's task is to guess a five-letter password in five attempts. A correctly guessed letter is highlighted in red, while a letter out of place is highlighted in yellow. The game contains a total of about 250 passwords to be guessed.

440601.overview: The player's task is to guess a five-letter password in five attempts within a certain time limit. A correctly guessed letter remains in the correct position, and a letter that appears in the password but in a different position is highlighted in red. The number of points scored depends on the time remaining after guessing the password.

440604.overview: A popular sports totalizator in which the player picks 6 digits. Each bet costs 2 coins and if the player hits at least one digit, he gets 3 coins. The more digits hit the more coins won.

441323.overview: There are 31 fish in the aquarium and in each of his turns the player can take 1, 2, 3 or 4 fish. The computer player does the same. To win, you must leave your opponent with one fish in your last turn.

442127.overview: The player's task is to move between two walls avoiding falling into holes. As you progress, the background color changes and the speed at which the walls are moved changes.

442167.overview: A strategic game in which the player's task is to colonize planets, extract resources, manage and defend against alien attacks. The game includes a random generator of planets, resources, galaxy sector layout and aliens. Each new game is a different approach to the challenges. At the beginning, you need to find a convenient planet to settle. To do this with a Pioneer-type ship, you should get as close as possible to the planet to explore it. Each planet is characterized by a different biome and resources. The game uses minerals needed for technological development, food for creating new ships (maximum 5) and energy used for assembling technology on ships. From time to time, aliens appear in the sector destroying the player's colonies, against which it is necessary to construct a sufficiently strong defense unit. In the factory you can build 10 different technological objects, which can be transferred to the ship you are creating. Colonization of dangerous planets requires protective clothing. The game also features tasks commissioned by the corporation, which must be completed. The trade drone allows you to sell raw materials collected in the warehouse, and if its color is green, you can trade with it.

442245.overview: A strategy game for two people in which four blocks of one color must be aligned horizontally, vertically or diagonally in any direction to win.

442348.overview: A card game of open-ended poker in which the player competes against three opponents for the highest winning stake in the pot. The first card is always face up and subsequent cards are added for the amount declared. As in any poker game, you can raise, wait or flip your cards. At the end, the last card is revealed and the one with the highest cards or figures wins and takes the whole pot.

442351.overview:
The player's task is to collect all the crosses on the board in the shortest possible time and with as few collisions with the walls as possible.

456406.overview:
2025 SEUCK Compo Entry #2

SCENARIO

The Master of Awesome, and his mentor the Master of Exposition, are heading for a breakdance competition. Not for money or glory, but to show off the physical feats of the School of Awesome as an example to the world. (And also because the alternative, spending a Saturday evening in the Temple of Awesome, was boring.)

Since they are running late and can't afford taxi or Uber, the Master of Awesome suggests they take a shortcut ... through the Ninja Zone.

THE NINJA ZONE! A (mostly peaceful) area of the city under complete ninja control. 4,000 extremely violent ninjas, dedicated to crime and stealthy murder, await anyone who tries to cross their turf. (They also carry an old grudge against the Temple of Awesome - see the original KUNG-FU MANIACS Trilogy.)

Thus begins the quest to reach the breakdancing competition in time. Will the School of Awesome's secret dance move - the Twerk of Destiny - save the day...?


HOW TO PLAY
 
This is a 1 or 2 player game. Press Fire on either joystick to start the game.

The second player can join in any time, by pressing Fire.

Joystick Port 2: Control the Master of Awesome
Joystick Port 1: Control the Master of Exposition

You earn a bonus life for every 10,000 points you score.

Press FIRE to strike. If you combine a strike with a jump, you can make various flying attacks.

The default direction of a strike is always forward (from left to right). To strike backwards, hold LEFT while pressing Fire repeatedly.

Holding LEFT also makes your character do the Twerk of Destiny - which doubles as a way to duck.


JUMPING
 
Press or hold UP to jump, and combine with LEFT/RIGHT to make a long jump.

The longer you hold LEFT or RIGHT, the longer the jump. You can change the direction of a jump - or break it - in midair.

If you keep holding UP, you will automatically jump again as soon as you land.

You can jump onto these objects - but only from the sides:
LEDGES, CRATES, STREETLAMPS, RAILS, TABLES, COUCHES, TREES, VANS and WALL PIPES.

IMPORTANT: If you find yourself "stuck" after you jump onto the very edge of an object, just keep holding UP to immediately make another jump and move on.

Blocks can be dropped from any side, and those already on the board will be moved if there is an empty space behind them. Each move has a time limit, and after it expires, the block will automatically be placed on the board. The game ends if a block is placed on a line where there is no space.

460283.overview: The game involves combining blocks of the same value to double their number. The blocks can be moved up/down and left/right. With each move, another block is added to the board. The game ends when there are no more moves possible or one of the blocks reaches a value of 8192.
